name: PAM8403
description: The PAM8403 is a 3W per channel filterless class-D stereo audio amplifier from Diodes Incorporated. Its filterless architecture drives speakers directly with no LC output filter, saving cost and board area, and reaches up to 90% efficiency for portable use. Each channel is a bridge-tied-load (BTL) output, so the speaker connects between the +OUT and -OUT pins of a channel with no connection to ground. It includes short-circuit protection, thermal shutdown, and low supply-voltage detection that mutes the outputs at about 2V. The fixed default gain is 24dB. Diodes lists it as not recommended for new design (successor PAM8406).

typical_application: Battery- or USB-powered portable stereo speaker driving two 4 to 8 ohm speakers directly with no output filter.
gotchas: Outputs are bridge-tied (BTL): wire each speaker between +OUT and -OUT of a channel; never connect an output to ground.
Both MUTE (pin 5) and SHND (pin 12) are active low; tie them high (to VDD) for normal operation.
This is the bare chip pinout; the common red PAM8403 amplifier board adds a volume pot, input/output headers, and decoupling, so its connector labels do not map directly to these pin numbers.
Filterless output is a high-frequency PWM square wave; keep speaker wires short and use ferrite beads for long runs to limit EMI.
Marked not recommended for new design by Diodes; PAM8406 is the suggested replacement.
